items.prompt: What is this spoon made of?

figure.alt: A brown wooden spoon with lines in the wood.

options.why: Glass is see-through and breaks easily.
A paper spoon would get soggy in food.

hints: Look at the colour and the lines on the spoon.
Which material comes from trees?
Think about a table or a door. What are they often made of?
items.explanation: This spoon is made of wood. Wood comes from trees and is hard and strong.

items.prompt: Match each object to the material it is made of.

figure.alt: Four objects: a window, a book, a sock and a nail.

hints: Think about how each object feels.
Do the ones you know first.
Start with the window. What material can you see through?
items.explanation: A window is made of glass, a book of paper, a sock of fabric and a nail of metal.

items.prompt: Is it metal or plastic? Sort the cards.
hints: Metal is hard and often shiny and cold to touch.
Think about how each object feels in your hand.
Start with the key. What is a key made of?
items.explanation: Keys, nails and paperclips are made of metal. The bottle, the comb and the toothbrush handle are made of plastic.

items.prompt: Which object is made of fabric?

options.why: A brick is made of baked clay.
Cups are often made of plastic or glass.

hints: Fabric is soft and bendy, like cloth.
Which object can you wear?
Look at your own clothes. What are they made of?
items.explanation: A T-shirt is made of fabric. Fabric is soft and bends easily, so it is good for clothes.

items.prompt: Windows are made of ___ so we can see through them.
hints: Think about what you look through at home.
This material is see-through and smooth.
It can break if a ball hits it.
items.explanation: Windows are made of glass. Glass is see-through, so light comes in and we can see outside.

items.prompt: Mr Joko makes a chair. Which material is good for it?

options.why: Paper is too weak. The chair would break.

hints: A chair must hold a person up.
Which material is hard and strong?
Think about the chairs in your classroom.
items.explanation: Wood is hard and strong, so it is a good material for a chair.

items.prompt: Choose all the things made of paper.
hints: Paper is thin and is made from trees.
Think about what you can write or draw on.
Start with the book. What are its pages made of?
items.explanation: Books, newspapers and birthday cards are made of paper. Windows are glass and nails are metal.

items.prompt: Rina's ball is bouncy and bendy. What is it most likely made of?

options.why: Glass is hard and can break when it is dropped.
A stone ball is heavy and hard. It does not bounce well.

hints: Think about which material is bendy and bouncy.
Bicycle tyres are made of this material too.
Squeeze each one in your mind. Which one squashes and springs back?
items.explanation: Bouncy balls are usually made of rubber. Rubber squashes when it hits the floor and springs back.

items.prompt: Which object is made of more than one material?

options.why: A marble is made of glass only.
A nail is made of metal only.

hints: Look for an object with different parts.
Think about each part of the object. Is it the same material?
Picture a pencil. What is the eraser made of? What is the outside made of?
items.explanation: A pencil with an eraser has wood on the outside, a grey writing part in the middle and a rubber eraser at the end.

items.prompt: Lestari wants a cup that will not break if it falls. Which material?

options.why: Glass cups can break when they fall.
Clay cups can crack or break when they fall.

hints: Think about what happens when each cup falls on the floor.
Which material bends a little instead of breaking?
Picture dropping each cup on a hard floor.
items.explanation: A plastic cup will not break if it falls. Glass and clay cups can crack or break.

items.prompt: Which two objects are made of the same material?

options.why: A book is paper. A sock is fabric.
A window is glass. A brick is baked clay.

hints: Name the material of each object.
Look for two objects with the same material name.
Start with the key. What is it made of?
items.explanation: A key and a nail are both made of metal. The other pairs are made of two different materials.

items.prompt: Some rubber comes from the sap of rubber trees. Is this rubber natural?

figure.alt: A rubber tree and a rubber band.

options.text: Yes, because it comes from a plant.

options.why: Being bendy does not tell us where a material comes from.

options.text: No, because it is made in a shop.
options.why: Shops sell rubber things. The rubber itself came from trees.

hints: Natural materials come from plants, animals or the ground.
Where does this rubber come from?
Think about the tree in the picture.
items.explanation: Rubber from rubber trees is a natural material because it comes from a plant. Indonesia grows many rubber trees.
